source.title: Are All Linear Regions Created Equal?
source.authors: Matteo Gamba; Adrian Chmielewski-Anders; J. Sullivan; Hossein Azizpour; Mårten Björkman

record.file_problem: Full paper and supplementary material supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures how model size and training conditions relate to test error, and measures properties of trained networks against that error. These are conceptual tests of V7's network-property/generalization-gap relationship and related size/generalization behavior, using absolute deviation and linear-region density rather than magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.gate_note: Results cited from prior work, including Zhang et al. (2018) on fitting random labels, are not rows. Rows record this study's own reported measures and outcomes. The paper studies CIFAR classifiers and model-wise double descent; it does not test most claim versions' specific interventions.
record.test_reason: Section 3.6 directly tests V2's width/generalization relationship in a new setting: ResNet18 on CIFAR-10 with 20% corrupted labels. Training error reaches zero at width 16, and further widening lowers test error while maintaining zero training error. Absolute deviation and region density do not test V7's magnitude-aware weight sharpness.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The authors conclude that unweighted linear-region density is a fragile complexity measure for trained ReLU networks, and that the second descent accompanies reduced nonlinearity and increased local similarity of regions. They explicitly present absolute deviation as a nonlinearity benchmark rather than a new generalization measure.
record.recipe_differences: Measures absolute deviation from endpoint affine interpolation and linear-region density along data-driven paths; V7 instead names magnitude-aware sharpness and compares it with norm- and margin-based measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Results vary with architecture, dataset, noise fraction, data augmentation, path construction, and model width. Density may increase or decrease with noisier labels depending on architecture; the paper reports different density behavior for VGG8 and ResNet18.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear-region density correlates weakly with absolute deviation and can respond inconsistently to label noise or augmentation across architectures.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Linear-region counts along data-driven input paths are an unreliable proxy for learned function nonlinearity.

fits_no_version.finding: Absolute deviation follows test error after interpolation, whereas density increases with width; across settings, similar density can accompany very different test errors.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Input-space function variation can track test error better than unweighted linear-region density in the tested networks.

record.peer_reviewed: International Conference on Artificial Intelligence and Statistics (AISTATS 2022), Proceedings of Machine Learning Research, Volume 151
record.problems: The property measurement is one-dimensional and depends on data-driven directions; the authors state it is not a novel generalization measure. Several results are supplied as figures without exact values in the text. Experiments cover VGG8 and ResNet18 on CIFAR datasets, not the full range of architectures or claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: Table 2 reports additional separately conditioned comparisons of absolute deviation and density across noisy-label fractions, architectures, datasets, and trained-versus-initialized networks. Kept representative VGG8 and ResNet18 cases plus the full correlation table and width sweep; additional paired-difference entries were omitted to remain within the row limit and because they repeat the same direction-of-effect result. Sections 3.4 and Supplementary F describe further per-path/trajectory comparisons, with some results only in figures.

untested.parts: The complete paired claim about natural-label held-out accuracy and chance-level random-label held-out accuracy under the same architecture and recipe is not established. Perfect noisy-label training fit alone is insufficient.
The original one-hidden-layer MNIST and downsampled-CIFAR-10 settings and training to convergence are not tested; the width experiment uses deep residual networks and a fixed 400-epoch budget.
Convolutional versus fully connected generalization, local connectivity, and convolution-derived initialization.
Controlled adaptive-optimizer versus SGD comparisons and tuning, decay, or switching interventions.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations of the training recipe.
Dropout interventions and joint removal of dropout and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight-perturbation sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and rankings against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removal of examples selected by memorization influence versus random removal, followed by retraining.

record.verdict_notes: The rise in test error before width 16 does not challenge V2's claim about widening after interpolation. Different architecture and fixed training duration define the tested setting; they do not themselves warrant a limits_scope verdict. The original V7 verdict confuses different constructs.

versions.untested_parts: Whether networks fitting random labels also generalize on natural labels, and random-label held-out accuracy.
Whether test error keeps falling as one-hidden-layer ReLU networks widen beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected test error and the role of local connectivity.
Comparative generalization of adaptive optimizers and SGD under different tuning or decay choices.
Batch-size effects on generalization under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Effects of adding or removing dropout and weight decay on held-out error.
Magnitude-scaled weight perturbation sharpness and comparisons to norm- and margin-based measures; the reported property is absolute deviation, not sharpness.
Removing memorized examples and retraining to measure test-accuracy change.

rows.subject: VGG8
rows.size_stated: 8 layers; 174116 parameters (CIFAR-10), 185006 (CIFAR-100)
rows.operation_detail: Measured median absolute deviation and density along data-driven paths across noisy-label fractions.
rows.measure: Median absolute deviation; median linear-region density
rows.uncertainty: Figure 5 reports averages over three runs; values figure only.
rows.note: No exact plotted values supplied in text. Text states absolute deviation almost always increases with harder problems; density increases with task complexity for VGG8.
rows.check: Neither measure is magnitude-aware weight sharpness. The source also contradicts itself about density: Figure 5's caption says VGG8 density increases with noise, whereas Sections 3.1–3.2 and Table 2 indicate the opposite. Preserve that ambiguity.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.size_stated: 18 layers; base width 16 in the general experiments
rows.operation_detail: Swept ResNet18 base width and measured train error, test error, absolute deviation, and density.

conditions.value: 400 epochs; Adam; base learning rate 1e − 4; no explicit regularization or data augmentation

rows.measure: Train and test error (0/1 loss), absolute deviation, and density across width
rows.value: Text reports train/test error fall for w ≤ 4, test error rises for 4 < w ≤ 16, zero train error and highest test error at w = 16, then test error descends for w > 16; absolute deviation peaks at w = 16 and decreases thereafter; density monotonically increases.
rows.uncertainty: Three seeds for Figure 2; no numeric uncertainty for these curves stated in text.
rows.note: The paper says this reproduces the model-wise deep double descent setting and reports the direction of each curve in text; exact curve values are not stated.
rows.check: Relink from V7 to V2. Section 3.6 explicitly reports decreasing test error for widths above 16 while training error remains zero. Split the train/test-error result from the absolute-deviation and density measures, which do not test V7.

source_check.locator_found: Section 3.6; Figure 2 caption; Supplementary Material A, Model-Wise Deep Double Descent.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.size_stated: 18 layers; widths through standard base width 64
rows.operation_detail: Compared test error with mean absolute deviation and mean density across experimental settings.
rows.measure: Mean test error against mean absolute deviation and mean density
rows.uncertainty: Means computed over three independent runs; no numerical uncertainty stated.
rows.note: Text reports absolute deviation better predicts test error and fixed density can correspond to vastly different test performance; figure values are not specified.
rows.check: Figure 6 covers all networks and experimental settings, including VGG8, rather than ResNet18 alone. It relates test error to input-space nonlinearity measures, not magnitude-aware sharpness to generalization gap.

relationships.display_finding: Further widening beyond the interpolation threshold reduced test error while preserving zero training error under the fixed training budget.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100 VGG8 and ResNet18 experiments using absolute deviation and density
reader_labels.reason: Absolute deviation relates to test error and rises/falls with model-wise double descent, but this is not magnitude-aware sharpness, and density correlations with absolute deviation are weak across settings (R3–R16, R20–R21).
